title: Packaged Drinking Water
summary: IS 14543 covers the specification for packaged (other than mineral) drinking water, including requirements for physical, chemical and microbiological quality, and packaging. Products sold under this category are commonly required to hold BIS certification (ISI mark) before sale in India.
applicability: Applies to packaged drinking water (other than natural mineral water) intended for human consumption.

details: Product must be tested at a BIS-recognised laboratory.

steps: Undergo sample testing at BIS-recognised lab or in-house lab.

next_actions: Identify the applicable standard.
Determine applicable certification.
Complete applicable testing.
Follow the applicable BIS certification process.
guidance: Manufacturers of packaged drinking water are generally required to obtain a BIS product certification licence and get their product tested at a BIS-recognised laboratory before using the ISI mark. Exact testing parameters and licensing steps should be confirmed with BIS directly.
source_name: BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) — publicly listed standard

title: Product Certification Scheme (ISI Mark)
summary: The BIS Product Certification Scheme allows manufacturers to obtain a licence to use the Standard Mark (ISI mark) on products that conform to the relevant Indian Standard. It is a third-party guarantee of quality, safety and reliability for consumers.
applicability: Applies to manufacturers seeking to use the ISI Mark on products conforming to Indian Standards.
requirements: Establishment of an in-house testing facility (in most cases)
Acceptance of the Scheme of Testing and Inspection (STI)

details: Sample testing required either at a BIS-recognised lab or in-house lab depending on the specific standard.

next_actions: Verify if product is under mandatory certification (QCO).
Ensure manufacturing premises has adequate testing facilities.
Apply through the official BIS CMS/e-BIS portal.
guidance: The typical process involves: applying to BIS, sample testing at a BIS-recognised or in-house lab, factory inspection, and grant of licence. Certain product categories fall under mandatory certification (e.g. via Quality Control Orders) while others are voluntary. Applicants should verify current requirements on the official BIS portal (CMS/e-BIS).

title: Hallmarking of Gold & Silver Jewellery
summary: Hallmarking is the official assaying and marking system for gold and silver jewellery/articles in India, administered by BIS. It certifies the purity/fineness of precious metal articles through Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs).
applicability: Applies to gold and silver jewellery and artifacts manufactured and sold in India.
requirements: Articles must be assayed and hallmarked at a BIS-recognised AHC.
Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) must be present on the article.

details: Assaying is conducted at BIS-recognised Assaying & Hallmarking Centres (AHCs).

steps: AHC assays and applies hallmark with HUID.

next_actions: Obtain BIS Registration for Jewellers.
Send articles to a recognised AHC for hallmarking.
Verify HUID via BIS Care app (for consumers).
guidance: Jewellers need BIS registration to sell hallmarked jewellery, and articles are assayed at a BIS-recognised Assaying & Hallmarking Centre. Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) is used for traceability. Exact caratage rules and applicability should be verified on the BIS Hallmarking portal.

title: BIS-Recognised Testing Laboratories
summary: BIS maintains a network of its own regional/branch laboratories and recognises select private/third-party laboratories for product testing under various certification schemes. Testing verifies whether a product sample conforms to the relevant Indian Standard.
applicability: Applies to products requiring sample testing for BIS certification.
requirements: Testing must be performed at an officially recognised BIS laboratory or branch laboratory.
Test reports must conform to the relevant IS standard.

details: Refer to the official BIS Lab Recognition scheme list for authorised labs.

next_actions: Check the BIS Care app or BIS portal for the current list of recognised labs by product and region.
Send samples to the appropriate lab as directed by the scheme.
guidance: The applicable laboratory depends on the product category and scheme. The official BIS website and BIS Care app list recognised labs by product and region — always confirm the current, region-specific list from BIS rather than relying on a fixed list, as recognitions can change.
keywords: where can i test my product

title: BIS Licensing for Manufacturers
summary: A BIS licence permits a manufacturer to apply the Standard Mark on a specific product manufactured at a specific location, after their product and process are found to conform to the applicable Indian Standard.
applicability: Applies to manufacturers seeking to apply the Standard Mark (ISI) on their products.
requirements: Manufacturing infrastructure capable of producing conforming products.
Adequate testing equipment as per standard.

details: Both in-house testing and third-party testing may be required.

next_actions: Ensure manufacturing location has necessary testing infrastructure.
Apply online via the BIS portal.
Prepare for factory audit and sample testing.
guidance: Applications are generally submitted online via the BIS portal, followed by document scrutiny, sample testing, and factory audit. Licence validity, renewal and surveillance (periodic) inspections follow BIS rules. Fee structure and timelines should be checked on the official portal as they may change.
keywords: how do i get bis licence

title: Consumer Complaints & Grievance Redressal
summary: BIS provides consumer-facing services including complaint registration for ISI-marked or hallmarked products that appear substandard, and general consumer awareness on Indian Standards through the BIS Care mobile app and portal.
applicability: Applies to consumers wishing to verify products or file complaints regarding BIS certified products.
requirements: Product must carry ISI mark or HUID for BIS verification.
next_actions: Download the BIS Care app.
Enter the license number or HUID to verify.
Lodge a complaint if the product appears substandard or counterfeit.
guidance: Consumers can verify a licence/HUID and lodge a complaint through the BIS Care app or the BIS website's grievance section. This prototype does not connect to the live BIS Care system.

title: Indian Standards — What They Are
summary: An Indian Standard is a document, established by consensus and approved by BIS, that provides rules, guidelines or characteristics for products, processes or services to ensure quality, safety and interoperability.
applicability: Applies generally to products, processes, and services in India.
next_actions: Search for specific standards on the official BIS Standards portal.
Purchase or access the full text of the standard.
guidance: Standards are identified by an IS number (e.g. IS 14543) and are developed by Technical Committees of BIS with stakeholder participation. The full text of standards is typically available for purchase/access via the official BIS Standards portal.

title: BIS Schemes Overview
summary: BIS operates multiple schemes depending on product/sector: Product Certification (ISI Mark), Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) for electronics/IT goods, Hallmarking for precious metals, and Management System Certification (ISO-type schemes).
applicability: Various schemes apply depending on the product category and sector.
requirements: Food and general products typically fall under Product Certification (ISI Mark).
next_actions: Identify the nature of the product.
Determine which scheme (e.g. CRS, ISI, Hallmarking) covers the product.
Follow the specific scheme's guidelines.
guidance: The applicable scheme depends on the product category — e.g. electronics typically fall under CRS, food/general products under Product Certification. Sample/demo mapping only — always confirm the correct scheme for a specific product with BIS.
